subject: Orchard Health — inference ops comparison & runbook for failovers
body:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@orchard.health>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@orchard.health>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Orchard Health — inference ops comparison & runbook for failovers

Dana / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single shared plan for the competitive reliability checks you asked for.

Summary of what we discussed:
- Objective: Validate failover behavior, rate-limit characteristics, and realistic error-budget impact when running a production inference flow (EMR-triggered batch + low-latency API for triage).
- Comparison targets: Redwood hosted inference (standard and fallback variants) vs two hyperscaler managed endpoints (Vendor A: Vertex-like; Vendor B: MajorCloud managed endpoints).
- Key signals to collect: P50/P95/P99 latency, tail token emission latency (first-byte / last-byte), rate-limit responses (429 patterns and retry-after header behavior), persistent error types, and error-budget burn over 24h sustained and burst windows.

Planned tests (see attached orchard_test_plan.xlsx):
1) Sustained ramp: 15 min ramp to 500 RPS sustained over 2 hours to measure steady-state latencies and token cost.
2) Burst stress: 60s bursts up to 1,200 RPS to surface queueing, token throttles, and any circuit-breaker behavior.
3) Regional failover: Simulate regional outage by blocking a single region for 10 minutes; measure automatic fallback time, success ratio, and cost delta.
4) Small-model fallback scenario: Force a fallback from redwood-llama-13b to redwood-llama-4b for degraded SLA recovery; observe quality regressions and throughput gain.
5) Long-context token storm: Run long-context (8k tokens) sessions to measure KV cache hit-rate and tail latency impact.

What Redwood will provide by EOD tomorrow (29 Jun):
- A draft runbook (runbook_failover_draft.md) with exact curl traffic generators, headers to capture (x-request-id, x-redwood-token-ops), and expected response codes.
- A helper script to collect P95/P99 for both token-level and response-level latencies and to normalize logs across vendors.
- Pre-configured rate-limit buckets to emulate your production token mix.

What we need from Orchard by Tue 30 Jun:
- Finalized test windows (preferred start times) and an owner for network/config changes (Evan or Priya).
- A representative prompt set and 5 sample callflows you run in prod (this helps with model fallback quality checks).
- Confirmation if we should include MajorCloud’s managed burst tier (they require a lead time).

Attachments: orchard_test_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet) | redwood_vs_hyperscaler_profiles.pdf (summary perf profiles) | runbook_failover_draft.md (initial runbook)

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0148

From: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@orchard.health>

Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 09:11:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Orchard Health — inference ops comparison & runbook for failovers

Thanks Karthik — that looks good. A few clarifying Qs from our ops team: 

1) Rate limits: can Redwood simulate both token-based and request-based throttles in the same run so we can see combined behavior? Specifically we want to know if retries are depositional (push load downstream) or if the client gets clear Retry-After headers.
2) Error budget: do you have tooling to translate observed 5xxs/429s into an error-budget burn metric we can correlate to our SLO (99.95 for throughput, 99.9 for tail latency)?
3) Failover time: what is typical cold-warm failover time from hosted to dedicated or cross-region? We need a ballpark to decide if we should implement client-side fallback first.

Also looping in Evan (ops) — Evan, can you confirm if you want the 2-hour sustained window to run overnight (01:00 - 03:00 local) or during prime hours?

Dana
Director of Platform Engineering
Orchard Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchard Health — inference ops comparison & runbook for failovers

Ben here — answering the ops Qs and adding a few technical constraints we should capture in the runbook: 

1) Rate limits: yes — the traffic generator we provide can apply both token-based throttles (tokens/sec, tokens/min) and request-based concurrency caps. It will surface 429s with Retry-After where the vendor exposes it; where vendors return opaque internal errors we’ll tag and surface them separately.

2) Error budget translation: we’ll provide a small script that converts the observed 5xx/4xx/429 counts into a burn rate given your SLOs. Example: if you define success as 2xx only, we compute error_budget_burn = (errors / total_requests) normalized to a 30d budget. We’ll produce time-series so you can visualize bursts vs sustained periods.

3) Failover time: for Redwood hosted -> cross-region fallback in our hosted product, the median failover completion for active sessions is typically 6–18s depending on KV cache warm-up and whether the client is preserving session affinity; P99s can hit ~45s in worst-case (cold cache). If you need sub-5s SLAs for failover we recommend client-side primary+secondary with sticky tokens plus the server-side fallback as a safety net.

4) Observability hooks: include x-redwood-session and x-kv-cache-hit headers in the runbook so we can separate cache-miss-induced tail latency from pure compute latency.

I’ve attached an initial vendor-profiles PDF summarizing observed steady-state throughput and tail latencies for the typical model classes (small 4b, medium 13b, large 70b-ish).

Ben
Principal Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

One more ask: can Redwood include a simulation of our bursty clinician UI pattern where short 1–2 token system calls spike concurrently with long context generation? We want to ensure the UI path is never starved.

Priya

Thanks all — final confirmations and next steps:
- Window: 01:00 - 03:00 ET on Thu, 1 Jul 2026 (Evan to toggle network for regional failover at 01:30 ET).
- Redwood deliverables by Wed EOD: updated runbook with concrete curl commands + traffic generator config; normalized telemetry script; vendor headers mapping.
- Orchard deliverables by Wed EOD: prompt set (Drive); network contact for toggles (Evan); decision on including MajorCloud managed burst tier.
- Owners: Redwood: Ben (test infra + telemetry), Marissa (runbook + SLO mapping), Sean (post-test analysis). Orchard: Priya (ops window), Evan (network execution), Dana (stakeholder).

Karthik — I’ll follow up with a DocuSign for the test access Agreeement (limited scope) if you want — that will expedite observations on MajorCloud endpoints.

If there are no objections I’ll schedule the run in HubSpot and post the test ticket to the Drive folder.

Thanks — looking forward to getting these data points.

Karthik
